clips.start_words: Your credit report looks at your credit cards
clips.send: A homebuyer sends this to a friend about to refinance, anxious that an old balance is quietly costing them a better rate.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says almost nobody knows this about their credit score.

Your card doesn't report your balance the day you pay the bill. It reports to the bureau 5 to 10 days before your statement cycle closes - while you're still carrying whatever you charged that month.

Put $1,000 on a $10,000 limit and pay it off later in full, and the bureau can still show that $1,000 sitting there, dragging your score down.

Pay the balance before your reporting date instead, and your score can jump 15 points almost overnight - the difference between a good mortgage rate and a declined application.

When did you last check your card's reporting date?
